id: confucian|liyun_duties_advantages_disasters|Benevolence on the part of the ruler
list_name: The things which men consider right (人義, ten duties), the things advantageous to men (人利) and the things disastrous to men (人患)
virtue: Benevolence on the part of the ruler
rubric_v1_gloss: "benevolence on the part of the ruler ... these ten are the things which men consider to be right"
source_scope: The ruler's side of ruler–minister; Li Yun frames the sage ruler's task.

teaching.quote: He must know men’s feelings, lay open to them what they consider right, show clearly to them what is advantageous, and comprehend what are their calamities.
teaching.citation: Li Ki, Book VII, Li Yun, section II §§18-19, James Legge, SBE 27 (1885), p. 379

teaching.quote: **with benevolence on the part of the ruler, and loyalty on that of the minister**; — these ten are the things which men consider to be right.
teaching.citation: Li Ki, Li Yun, section II §§19-20, James Legge, SBE 27 (1885), p. 380

limits: 君仁 is named, not defined here.

list_name: The things which men consider right (人義, ten duties), the things advantageous to men (人利) and the things disastrous to men (人患)
rubric_v1_gloss: "Truthfulness in speech and the cultivation of harmony constitute what are called ‘ the things advantageous to men.’ ... and the maintenance of har¬ mony"
source_scope: Second of Li Yun's two things advantageous to men; paired with putting away quarrelling.

teaching.quote: **Truthfulness in speech and the cultivation of harmony constitute what are called ‘ the things advantageous to men.’** ... promote truthfulness of speech, and the maintenance of harmony ; show his value for kindly consideration and complaisant courtesy; and put away quarrelling and plundering,
teaching.citation: Li Ki, Li Yun, section II §§19-20, James Legge, SBE 27 (1885), p. 380

limits: Term undefined; harmony is not mere silence or compliance.

list_name: The things which men consider right (人義, ten duties), the things advantageous to men (人利) and the things disastrous to men (人患)
virtue: Deference on the part of juniors
rubric_v1_gloss: "deference on that of juniors ... these ten are the things which men consider to be right"
source_scope: The junior's side of the elder–junior pair in Li Yun's ten.

teaching.quote: kindness on the part of elders, **and deference on that of juniors**; ... — these ten are the things which men consider to be right. ... show his value for kindly consideration and complaisant courtesy;
teaching.citation: Li Ki, Li Yun, section II §§19-20, James Legge, SBE 27 (1885), p. 380

teaching.explanation: 幼順 is undefined; juniors relative to elders, kin or not.

limits: Ordinary politeness to strangers is not automatically this role duty; seniority relation is needed.

id: confucian|liyun_duties_advantages_disasters|Filial duty on the part of the son
list_name: The things which men consider right (人義, ten duties), the things advantageous to men (人利) and the things disastrous to men (人患)
virtue: Filial duty on the part of the son
rubric_v1_gloss: "filial duty on that of the son ... these ten are the things which men consider to be right"
source_scope: The son's side of the father–son pair; Xiaojing's wrong-command teaching is separately attributed.

teaching.quote: What are ‘ the things which men consider right ? ’ **Kindness on the part of the father, and filial duty on that of the son**;
teaching.citation: Li Ki, Book VII, Li Yun, section II §§18-19, James Legge, SBE 27 (1885), p. 379

teaching.quote: — **these ten are the things which men consider to be right.**
teaching.citation: Li Ki, Li Yun, section II §§19-20, James Legge, SBE 27 (1885), p. 380

teaching.quote: “When the command is wrong, a son should resist his father, and a minister should resist his August Master. “The maxim is, ‘Resist when wrongly commanded.’ **Hence how can he be called filial who obeys his father when he is commanded to do wrong?**”
teaching.citation: Classic of Filial Piety, chapter XV, Ivan Chen, The Book of Filial Duty (1908)

limits: Li Yun does not define the duty. Xiaojing is related teaching; Mencius 4B30 on reproof differs and is unresolved here.

teaching.explanation: 兄良 is named, not explained.

teaching.explanation: 長惠 is named, not defined; elders may be nonkin seniors.

teaching.citation: LiKi BookVII LiYun§19, Legge1885, pp379–380

limits: 奪 is named, not defined; no source narrative.

list_name: The things which men consider right (人義, ten duties), the things advantageous to men (人利) and the things disastrous to men (人患)
rubric_v1_gloss: "Quarrels, plundering, and murders are ‘ the things disastrous to men.’ ... and put away quarrelling and plundering"
source_scope: First of Li Yun's three things disastrous to men; a general list, not each duty's negation.

teaching.quote: **Quarrels, plundering, and murders are ‘ the things disastrous to men.’** Hence, when a sage (ruler) would ... put away quarrelling and plundering, if he neglect the rules of propriety, how shall he succeed ?
teaching.citation: Li Ki, Li Yun, section II §§19-20, James Legge, SBE 27 (1885), p. 380

limits: 爭 is named, not defined. Calm disagreement or remonstrance is not automatically a quarrel.

teaching.quote: A faithful minister, if his monarch does wrong reproves him ; **a virtuous wife, in the same way, tells her husband when he is in fault, and aids him to do better.** A really superior man does not desire flattery from his wife, but her true words are precious.
teaching.citation: Typical Women of China, Woman’s WordschII, trSafford1891, p92

limits: Historical hierarchy attributed only. Safford's reproof teaching is a later text, not Li Yun's own words.

Hence, when a sage (ruler) would ... promote truthfulness of speech, and the maintenance of harmony ; ... if he neglect the rules of propriety, how shall he succeed ?
